structure: Theodosian land walls (triple line: outer wall; terrace; inner wall; moat)
construction_period: Built 412-413; rebuilt after the 447 earthquake collapse; maintained and repaired for a millennium
length_note: 5.7 km is given for the main triple line; 6670 m appears in one source that appears to include the northern Blachernae extension to the Golden Horn.
condition_1453: Repaired shortly before the siege (1439 inscription cited at Silivrikapi) but under sustained bombardment from 6 April 1453
conflict_note: Tower counts vary by source: one gives 96 inner plus 92 outer (188 total); another counts 192 total. Height and thickness are ranges across the outer wall (lower, thinner) and inner wall (higher, thicker). Do not present a single number as exact.

structure: Sea walls along the Golden Horn
construction_period: Byzantine era; extended and repaired over centuries
length_note: Length not independently found in the sources reviewed; treated as N/A.
condition_1453: Single-line wall, described by multiple sources as weaker than the land walls
conflict_note: No dimension figures found in the sources reviewed for this project; only qualitative 'weaker than the land walls' claims are supported.

structure: Sea walls along the Sea of Marmara
construction_period: Byzantine era; extended and repaired over centuries
length_note: Length not independently found in the sources reviewed; treated as N/A.
conflict_note: No dimension figures found in the sources reviewed for this project.

construction_period: Constructed later than the main Theodosian line; single wall, not triple
length_note: Length not independently found in the sources reviewed.
condition_1453: Described as a weaker, single-wall sector; associated with the Kerkoporta postern
conflict_note: Only qualitative description found; no dimension figures.

construction_period: Installed at the start of the 1453 siege
length_note: A commonly repeated span of about 750 m is not independently verified in the Tier-1/Tier-2 sources reviewed for this project; treated as unverified and excluded from any chart.
condition_1453: Held against a direct Ottoman naval assault on 11-12 April 1453; bypassed on 22 April when ships were hauled overland into the harbour
conflict_note: Length figure is widely repeated online but not confirmed in this project's Tier-1/Tier-2 sources; do not chart.

length_note: N/A (point fortress, not a wall line)
condition_1453: Completed a full winter before the siege; garrisoned and armed with cannon covering the strait
conflict_note: Tower/gate counts vary: 3 main towers plus 1 small plus 13 secondary in one source; 3 main plus 12 secondary (15 total) in another.

condition_1453: Pre-existing fortress used in tandem with Rumelihisari to blockade the strait in 1453

construction_period: Gate is Byzantine era (Theodosian); Yedikule fortress added by the Ottomans in 1458
condition_1453: Ceremonial/Byzantine triumphal entrance; became an Ottoman fortress-treasury-prison after 1458
